findings.title: A common witnessed reckoning gathers divergent parties
findings.claim: The ayah's divided parties can be heard as taking separate positions now and being brought into one witnessed, overwhelming encounter on the named great day.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers ٱخْتَلَفَ, كَفَرُوا۟, مَّشْهَدِ, and عَظِيمٍ supply divergent direction, religious rejection, direct presence and seeing, and heavy catastrophe. The wider surfaces in 43:65, 51:60, 11:103, and 83:5 independently return those relations through matching dispute, woe, gathering and witnessing, and great-day contacts, changing the warning into a shared public reckoning.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the ayah places factional fracture beside the great day: the disagreement remains socially divided while the named scene gathers all sides into one visible consequence.
findings.containment: This adds a public future consequence to the plain report that factions differ and disbelievers face woe. It does not identify the historical factions, make every root-family sense active, or turn the focus into a general judgment on all disagreement.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication is trusted and anchored to four focus words; its wider connection targets provide exact Arabic surfaces but no target morphology, so the global synthesis remains qualified.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Taraflar aynı yolu veya tutumu izlemek yerine birbirinden ayrı yönler tutar.
branch_activations.carrier: The perfect Form VIII verb ٱخْتَلَفَ reports the parties' completed divergence.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 43:65 surface repeats party divergence and places woe beside a coming day.
branch_activations.activation: The wider recurrence makes the focus divergence a taking of separate directions within a common dispute, rather than an unbounded difference.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The parties' disagreement is seen as a socially embodied split carried toward one public reckoning.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not name the parties' historical identities or activate every خ ل ف branch.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Those who reject the preceding religious claim are named as the target of woe at the promised encounter.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus's k-f-r carrier remains religious rejection here; physical covering, ingratitude, and other root-family senses are not activated.

branch_activations.activation: The wider gathered-and-witnessed day meets the focus noun's presence-and-seeing sense and makes the future scene common to the disputants.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The coming day is perceived as a scene in which the divided parties are present together and see its consequence.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus keeps مَّشْهَدِ as a scene of presence and seeing; it does not thereby become a legal testimony formula.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Ani ya da ağır biçimde başa gelen şiddetli bir felaket söz konusudur.
branch_activations.carrier: The indefinite genitive adjective عَظِيمٍ gives the day overwhelming scale and consequence.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 83:5 surface names a great day, while 51:60 attaches woe to the promised day of those who reject belief.
branch_activations.activation: Together the wider great-day and woe surfaces make greatness a pressure of consequential difficulty around the focus scene, not a measure of physical size alone.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The day is felt as an overwhelming and hard-to-escape catastrophe for the people named under woe.
branch_activations.boundary: The adjective does not by itself specify physical magnitude or activate the other ʿ-ẓ-m dictionary branches.

findings.title: The factions take shape as coalitions
findings.claim: The definite plural ٱلْأَحْزَابُ can also be heard as concrete human coalitions organized around positions they hold.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun names recognizable parties. The exact 30:32 connection independently describes religious division and then gives each ḥizb what it holds as its distinguishing position. That contact activates the core party sense together with its shared-position specialization and returns through 19:37:2:2.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the disagreement embodied in groups with a held stance, rather than as an abstract label for difference.
findings.containment: The focus plural remains a reference to factions and adds their social shape. It does not identify specific communities or activate the share, reading-section, or military facets.

epistemic.reason: The exact target Arabic supplies the party-and-held-position contact, but the connection carries no trust label and no target morphology; the qualified branch status remains visible.

findings.title: The interval becomes a judgment space
findings.claim: The phrase describing what is between them can also be heard as the relational space in which their disputed matter is finally brought before judgment.
findings.mechanism: The focus preposition مِنْ and noun بَيْنِهِمْ locate the divergence within the relation among the parties. The exact 32:25 connection independently places God's separating judgment between disputants on the Day of Resurrection over what they differ about, returning that between-space to 19:37:4:1.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel among them as more than a neutral location: it becomes the space where the disagreement is exposed to a final decision.
findings.containment: The local phrase remains a location of disagreement and does not itself state God's judgment. The wider connection activates this judgment-space resonance without exhausting the other meanings of بَيْن.

epistemic.reason: The exact target Arabic directly supplies between-disputants, judgment, resurrection, and disagreement, while target morphology and a connection trust label are absent.

branch_activations.activation: The wider judgment-between-disputants relation meets the focus's between-space and gives that relation a final public consequence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The phrase's relational interval carries the image of a place where the parties' dispute is finally decided.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not itself name the judge or promise the exact wider sequence; other ب ي ن branches remain outside this activation.

findings.title: Divergence after disclosure
findings.claim: The factional split can also be felt as divergence occurring after knowledge has arrived, giving the disagreement the pressure of a response to disclosed truth.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier ٱخْتَلَفَ reports parties taking separate directions. The exact 45:17 connection presents clear signs and arrived knowledge before describing their disagreement and God's judgment, so the wider sequence returns through 19:37:1:2 and adds a temporal and ethical contour.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader perceives the fracture as a split that follows available clarification, rather than as mere coexistence of opinions.
findings.containment: The focus itself does not state this temporal order or assign the motive named in the wider verse. The focus's ordinary report of disagreement remains intact as this qualified wider resonance is added.

epistemic.reason: The connection supplies an exact Arabic sequence linking knowledge, disagreement, and judgment, but its target morphology and trust label are absent.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Taraflar aynı yolu veya tutumu izlemek yerine birbirinden ayrı yönler tutar.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus verb ٱخْتَلَفَ presents the parties as taking divergent directions.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 45:17 surface places clear signs and arrived knowledge before the report that they differed and before God's judgment between them.
branch_activations.activation: The wider order lets the focus's route-divergence be heard as a split that follows disclosure, adding response to available knowledge to the ordinary disagreement.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's disagreement is perceived as a fracture after clarification, carried alongside a future judgment.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not independently assert the wider temporal order or the wider verse's motive; this is a qualified resonance.

findings.title: The scene becomes public testimony
findings.claim: The noun مَّشْهَدِ can also be felt as a public testimony scene where disputed positions become accountable before witnesses.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun names the scene from which the woe is specified. The exact 39:69 connection brings prophets and witnesses before a judgment carried out with truth, returning that public witness relation through 19:37:9:1 and adding accountable testimony to mere presence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the coming scene as one in which facts and claims are publicly brought forward, not only as an event that people happen to witness.
findings.containment: The focus noun remains a witnessing scene and does not itself name witnesses, a legal formula, or every sh-h-d usage. The testimony aspect is a qualified wider addition.

epistemic.reason: The exact target surface names witnesses and judgment, but target morphology and a connection trust label are not supplied.
